substitutes.name: Pipistrel Sinus
substitutes.note: Self-launching. When substituted, the paired tow plane disappears too — engine on only for first ~2 min of flight.

substitutes.name: Winch launch
substitutes.powertrain: Ground-based winch (electric or diesel — noise is local to airfield, not propagated)
substitutes.note: Substitutes the tow-segment portion below the cutoff AGL — applies only to that sub-segment, not the whole track.

substitutes.name: ATP rule rollback (250 hr restricted-ATP)
substitutes.note: Restoring the pre-2013 commercial-to-ATP pathway at 250 hr would cut industry-driven hour-building flights by ~60% at full uptake. Slider value 0..100 maps to 0..60% reduction in training tracks at the listener. No airframe change — these tracks simply disappear because the regulatory demand for them disappears.
substitutes.policy_cost_note: Net per-pilot training cost drops ~$50k (1500hr@$150 → 500hr@$150 + R-ATP fees). Cost to the noise model is $0; cost to the regulatory conversation is political.
substitutes.advocacy_capex_note: Approximate cost of a multi-year FAA rulemaking advocacy campaign (industry group dues, expert testimony, legal review). One-time, shared across all proponents.

substitutes.name: Expanded simulator credit (200 hr toward ATP)
substitutes.note: Today (14 CFR 61.65) ATP candidates can credit up to 100 hr of full-motion simulator time against the 1500 hr requirement; restricted-ATP graduates of 4-yr aviation programs can credit up to 200 hr in some combinations. Expanding the general cap to 200 hr (or further toward EASA's 250 hr cap) would shift ~30% of in-air training onto sims. Slider value 0..100 maps to 0..30% reduction in training tracks at the listener.
substitutes.regulatory_action: FAA Part 61 rulemaking + per-school simulator capex
substitutes.cap_ex_note: Per-school cost of a Level 5+ FTD (flight training device). Roughly $350k for a fixed-base FTD that satisfies the expanded credit; full-motion Level D sims are $5M+ and not realistic for small school fleets.
substitutes.op_savings_per_hr_note: Net per-training-hour delta when an hour shifts from plane ($200/hr wet) to sim ($150/hr). School saves ~$50/hr on the substituted portion but has to absorb the FTD capex.
substitutes.policy_cost_note: Net per-pilot cost roughly +$5k (sim time is cheaper per hour but the FTD has to be amortized over a smaller hour pool than a fleet plane).
